name.value: Ancient Forest / Chun T'oh Whudujut Provincial Park

description.value: Ancient Forest / Chun T'oh Whudujut Provincial Park protects a portion of the only inland temperate rainforest in the world, located on Highway 16 midway between Prince George and McBride. Touring cyclists can explore thousand-year-old western redcedars via a 450-metre universal access boardwalk and an additional 2.3 km of boardwalk leading to old-growth giants and a cascading waterfall. The park sits in the traditional territory of the Lheidli T'enneh and is considered one of BC's must-see hiking destinations.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A world-unique inland temperate rainforest on the Yellowhead Highway 16 cycling corridor, with a universally accessible boardwalk — a compelling and verifiable stop for touring cyclists despite the absence of on-site water.
enrichment_extras.notes: No overnight camping is permitted at the Ancient Forest parking lot; the nearest camping is Purden Lake Park, approximately 50 km west.
